The test image shows a green leaf with multiple dark gray/black irregular lesions scattered across the surface, along with some white granular/powdery material on the leaf. The spots are irregular in shape and appear necrotic.

Key features:
- Dark gray/black irregular spots on leaf
- White powdery/granular material on leaf surface
- No obvious yellow halos around spots
- Leaf remains green background

Top candidates: Powdery_Mildew (white powdery coating + dark necrotic spots), Bacterial_Speck (small black spots), Septoria_Leaf_Blotch (tan/gray spots).

The combination of dark necrotic spots with white powdery material is most suggestive of Powdery_Mildew. Let me view one reference image.

The reference image for Powdery_Mildew shows white circular powdery patches on tomato leaves (early stage). The test image differs - it shows predominantly dark gray/black irregular spots with some scattered white granular material.

Comparing evidence:
- Test image: dark irregular necrotic spots + scattered white granular material on leaf
- Powdery mildew (early): white powdery circular patches
- The dark spots with white material could be advanced powdery mildew where lesions have become necrotic while white spore masses remain
- The symptom description states: "white powdery sporulation in round spots that begin small but expand and converge...lesions that become necrotic"
- The scattered white granular/powdery material across the leaf surface is consistent with powdery mildew sporulation
- No yellow halos visible (rules against Bacterial_Speck), no concentric rings (rules against Early_Blight), no tan/gray centers (less likely Septoria)

The combination of dark necrotic spots (advanced infection) with scattered white powdery granules on an otherwise green leaf best fits advanced-stage Powdery_Mildew.
